questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some teachers are graduates.

Some graduates are females.

All females are women.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some females are teachers.

II. Some women are teachers.

III. All women are females.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
**Statements:**

Some teachers are graduates.

Some graduates are females.

All females are women.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a11778ad46bcc7f118ddfe14e27d202df113a73d3e9e900d33fa509ddb1633e.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some females are teachers → False (There is no direct relation given between females and teachers so it can be possible but not definite)

II. Some women are teachers → False (There is no direct relation given between women and teachers so it can be possible but not definite)

III. All women are females → False (because all females are women but all women are also females it is not definite)

Hence, **“****None of the conclusions follow”.**

questions.question: If 14 * 64 = 39, 25 * 37 = 31 and 9 * 17 = 13, then what will be 52 * 46?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

(14 ÷ 2) + (64 ÷ 2) = 39;

(25 ÷ 2) + (37 ÷ 2) = 31,

(9 ÷ 2) + (17 ÷ 2) = 13

Similarly,

= (52 ÷ 2) + (46 ÷ 2)

= 26 + 23

= 49

Hence, the correct answer is 49.

questions.question:
In each question below is given a statement followed by two courses of action numbered I and II. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the suggested courses of action logically follow(s) for pursuing.

Statement: Students are found spending too much time on video games.

Course of Action I: Ban mobile games.

Course of Action II: Encourage students to engage in outdoor activities.
questions.solution:
Given:

Statement:

Students are found spending too much time on video games.

Action:

1.Ban mobile games – Does not follow (Because, banning games is an extreme measure and may not effectively solve the problem. It doesn’t address the underlying issue of time management or habits.)

2.Encourage students to engage in outdoor activities – **Follows** (Because, promoting outdoor activities provides a healthy alternative and directly helps reduce excessive gaming time.)

So, Only 2 follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

questions.question:
Consider the following sequence:

5 1 1 5 1 4 7 5 1 2 8 4 1 4 7 8 6 8 6 9 1 4 7 9 5 2 

How many such numbers are present in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by its factor and followed by an even number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Factors are natural numbers by which a larger number can be fully divided leaving no remainder.

Even numbers are divisible by 2.

Given sequence:

5 1 1 5 1 4 7 5 __**1 2 8 4**__ 1 4 7 8 6 8 6 9 1 4 7 9 5 2

There are only two such numbers: 2 and 8 obtained from the two combinations (1 2 8) and (2 8 4) respectively.

 
• (1 **2** 8) → 1 is a factor of 2 and 2 is followed by the even number 8.
 
• (2 **8** 4) → 2 is a factor of 8 and 8 is followed by the even number 4.

Hence, “**two**” is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a row of girls, Shweta is 11th from the right end. Mansi is 14th to the left of Shweta. If Mansi is 12th from the left end, then how many girls are there in the row?
questions.solution:
1) Shweta is 11th from the right end.

2) Mansi is 14th to the left of Shweta, that means Mansi is (11 + 14) = 25th from the right end.

3) If Mansi is 12th from the left end then, then total number of girls in the row = 25 + 12 - 1 = 36

Hence, there are total 36 girls in the row.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)

(7, 4, 56)

(8, 3, 48)
questions.solution:
**Logic : {First number × (Second number × 2)} = Third number.**

(7, 4, 56) → 7 × (4 × 2) ⇒ 7 × 8 = 56

And,

(8, 3, 48) → 8 × (3 × 2) ⇒ 8 × 6 = 48

Similarly,

**(9, 10, 180) → 9 × (10 × 2) ⇒ 9 × 20 = 180**

Hence, the **correct answer** is **"Option 4".**

questions.question: Among A, B, C, D, E, F and G each one of the them have different weight, G is lighter than only C. As many people are heavier than B equals to the number of people lighter than A. E is lighter than both B and A but heavier than F. D is heavy than both A and F. Then who is the third lightest person?
questions.solution:
Given :

 
• Seven people - A, B, C, D, E, F and G.
 
• Each one of the them have different weight.

​Explanation :

1) G is lighter than only C.

C > G > _ > _ > _ > _ > _

2) E is lighter than both B and A but heavier than F.

3) As many people are heavier than B equals to the number of people lighter than A.

 
• Case - 1 ⇒ C > G > B > _ > A > E > F
 
• Case - 2 ⇒ C > G > A > _ > B > E > F

4) D is heavy than both A and F.

As D is heavy than both A and F therefore case - 2 is eliminated.

 

 
• Case - 1 ⇒ **C > G > B > D > A > E > F**

Thus, according to the final arrangement A is the third lightest person.

Hence, "A" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
A question is given, followed by two statements labelled I and II. Identify which of the statements is/are sufficient to answer the question.

Shakuntala was born in the year 2016. What is her exact date of birth?

**Statements:**

(I) Shakuntala’s birth date is a prime number greater than 23.

(II) Shakuntala was born in a month having the least number of days.

options.text: (I) alone is sufficient while (II) alone is not sufficient.
(II) alone is sufficient while (I) alone is not sufficient.
Either (I) alone or (II) alone is sufficient.

questions.solution:
Statement (I): Shakuntala’s birth date is a prime number greater than 23- A month of a year has 30 or 31 days. So, a number being prime greater than 23 and less than or equal to 31, will be either 29 or 31.

Statement (II) Shakuntala was born in a month having the least number of days- The month with the least number of days is February, having only 28 days or 29 days (in a leap year).

Based on the above statements, Shakuntala's date of birth will be 29th February 2016.

Therefore, both statements are required for this.

Hence, the correct answer is "option 2".
